title: fix(app-shell): Studio's Interfaces rail closes nav editing when the package answers read-only, so no edit is taken on screen that its autosave will refuse (objectui#11167)
body:
Fixes #11167

Clause-②: no

## What

Studio's Interfaces pillar now closes nav editing when the package's write state answers `writable: false`, and puts back any unsaved nav edit taken before that answer. The toggle's documented "unknown writability stays ungated" behaviour is kept: while the package list is in flight, the toggle is still on offer.

## The defect (verified on `origin/main` `3ab51503b` before building)

- `StudioDesignSurface` holds `pkgWritable` tri-state (`undefined` while asking, `null` when it could not find out). `readOnly` is `pkgWritable === false`, and `readOnlySettled` is `pkgWritable !== undefined`, both handed to `InterfacesPillar`. Confirmed.
- In `InterfacesPillar`, `editNav` had two writers: the toggle's `onClick` (it flips `editNav` and calls `setNavSel(null)`) and the deep link's `onApply` (`if (enterEditing) setEditNav(true)`). Nothing turned it off on a read-only answer. Confirmed.
- The deep link's apply already gates on the write state. The pillar passes `readOnly: readOnlySettled ? readOnly : undefined` to `useNavSelDeepLink`, which waits while that is `undefined` and applies with `enterEditing: readOnly === false`. So the link never opens editing on a read-only package; the gap was only an editing session opened before the answer.
- The nav autosave is `blocked: !appName || !editNav || !!navSaving || readOnly`. Confirmed.
- Measured through ablation leg 1 below: with the new effect removed, the toggle hides after `writable: false`, but the canvas's "Add nav item" stays on screen.

## The change (`InterfacesPillar` only)

One effect keyed on `readOnly`, `editNav` and `navDirty`. When `readOnly` is true:

- If nav editing is open, it closes the way the toggle closes it: `editNav` goes false and `navSel` null. The nav-item inspector (it renders on `editNav && navSel`) closes with them. That is the whole of the toggle's close path; it resets nothing else.
- If the nav buffer is dirty, it is put back to a baseline and `navDirty` is cleared. The baseline (`navBaselineRef`) is the app document as last loaded (beside the load's `setAppDraft(body)`) or last saved (the nav save now records the document it sent).

**Unsaved edits taken in the window: discarded, deliberately.** An edit whose 1.5 s autosave debounce had not run out when the answer arrived was never sent: the blocked autosave clears its timer. The toggle's close keeps a dirty buffer, but on a writable package that buffer still has an autosave to reach when editing reopens. On a read-only package it has none, and the server refuses authoring anyway. Kept, the edit would sit in the rail's view-mode tree as if it were the package's navigation. `navDirty` would also hold the surface's leave guard (`beforeunload` and the header's confirm) and the copilot refresh hold for good. The card asks that no edit is left on screen unsaved, so the buffer is put back. An edit whose debounce had run out was sent while the state was unknown; the server's refusal surfaces as the pillar's existing error, and the put-back still leaves nothing unsaved on screen.

**One writer, one flag.** The effect reads the same `readOnly` prop the deep link reads. It is declared before `useNavSelDeepLink` on purpose. Effects run in declaration order, and the answer that closes editing is the same answer that settles a pending `?sel=nav:` link. So the link applies after the close, and its read-only selection (objectui#11153) survives. The ordering is pinned (ablation leg 2).

**Deep link, then read-only.** A link opens editing on a writable package, and a read-only answer follows (a package switch keeps the pillar mounted). That session closes through the same effect. Pinned at the pillar level.

## Pins

`StudioDesignSurface.navEditClosesOnReadOnly-11167.test.tsx`, five cases, each read-only case with a writable control:

1. Whole surface: Edit clicked while the package list is in flight, an item added, then `writable: false`. Editing closes, the toggle hides, the added item is nowhere on screen, and the leave guard lets go.
2. Control: the same, then `writable: true`. Editing stays open and the edit reaches a save (read after the save's re-read lands).
3. Whole surface: a pending `?sel=nav:nav_landing` link, with editing opened and an item selected in the window, then `writable: false`. Editing closes and the URL keeps `sel=nav:nav_landing`.
4. Pillar: a link that opened editing, re-rendered read-only. Editing and the linked item's inspector close.
5. Control: a writable re-render leaves it open.

objectui#11164's race pin file (`StudioDesignSurface.navDeepLink-11153.test.tsx`) is unmodified (`git diff --quiet` against the base exits 0) and green.

## Verification (at `7c7f285d5`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/`: Test Files 73 passed (73), Tests 414 passed (414).
- `pnpm exec turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...' --concurrency=2`: 28 of 28 tasks successful. Then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists the new pin file.
- `pnpm exec eslint` on the two changed source files: 0 errors, and 18 warnings. They are the same 18 as the base file's, each shifted by the lines inserted above it.
  - This is a declared narrowing; the repo-wide lint is CI's.
  - Population: both files were linted and none was ignored (`--format json` reports 2 files).
  - Linting is not type-aware (no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService` in `eslint.config.js`), so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.
- These gates all exit 0: `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `pnpm check:control-bytes`, `pnpm check:new-line-citations`, `pnpm check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:changeset-claims` and `check:pending-changeset-literals`.

**Ablation.** Run with `ablation-replace.mjs`, with the fix committed first. The subject is imported by relative path from `src`, so there is no `dist/` leg. Both legs ran the new pin file plus the objectui#11153 file:

- Leg 1, the effect deleted: 3 failed, 8 passed. The three read-only pins fail, each on `navEditingOpen()` staying true (the card's defect). Both controls and all six objectui#11153 pins stay green. Restored: the blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- Leg 2, the effect moved after `useNavSelDeepLink`: 1 failed, 10 passed. Only pin 3 fails, on `selParam()`: the close cleared the link's selection. Restored the same way.

## Acceptance notes

- No notice is shown when an unsaved nav edit is put back. A toast would need new strings in every locale pack, outside this card's file surface. The surface's own read-only posture (toggle hidden, Publish disabled with the read-only hint) is what the author sees.
- The toggle's "Done" also keeps a dirty buffer while its autosave is blocked on `!editNav`. What that leaves on a writable package is measured in the dev report's findings, not changed here.
- The first commit's message carries a plain `Part of objectui#11167` body line. It is neither a trailer nor a closing keyword, and the branch is not rewritten (objectui forbids force-push).
- No docs page describes nav editing on a read-only package, so no docs change is owed.
